planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6 weeks before the last frost; transplant into warm soil after all frost danger passes and stake or cage the vines.

directions: A French heirloom prized for its abundant clusters of smooth, round, apricot-orange fruits about 2-3 ounces each, with thin skin and a balanced, fruity-sweet flavor often compared to a ripe apricot. Start seed indoors 6 weeks before the last frost, transplant into warm, fertile soil, and stake or cage the vigorous indeterminate vines, which crop heavily and hold up well through Gulf South heat. Pick fruit as soon as it colors fully to keep the thin skins from splitting after summer rain, and expect steady production from early summer until frost.
sources: Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds Variety Catalog

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6 weeks before the last frost; give plants a long, warm growing season and sturdy staking, since the fused fruit clusters are heavier and more awkward than a normal tomato truss.

directions: A German novelty heirloom grown less for yield than for its bizarre fruit form: individual tomato segments fuse together as they develop into a lobed, rose- or brain-like cluster that can be broken apart by hand into bite-sized pieces, each with its own thin skin. The red-orange fruit is thin-walled and only moderately flavorful, so Reisetomate is best treated as a conversation-piece crop for gardeners with room for a vigorous, heavy-vining indeterminate plant rather than a primary sauce or slicing tomato. It needs a full, warm season to size up and is most reliable where summers are long and hot, making it a good fit for a Gulf South vegetable garden with space to spare.
sources: Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds Variety Catalog

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6 weeks before the last frost; transplant into warm soil after frost danger passes and stake the vigorous, potato-leaved vines.

directions: Collected from a Himalayan village garden, this heirloom is distinguished by soft, blue-green, potato-leaf foliage and heavy clusters of smooth, pink-red, medium-large globe fruits with few seeds and a rich sweet-tart flavor. The vigorous indeterminate vines are reliably productive through hot, humid conditions and have shown good foliage disease tolerance in Gulf South trial gardens compared to many other pink heirlooms. Stake or cage plants well, since the potato-leaf vines are dense and heavy once fruit sets, and pick at full color for the best flavor.
sources: Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds Variety Catalog

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6 weeks before the last frost; this fast-maturing Siberian heirloom tolerates cooler soil and air temperatures at transplant time better than most cherry tomatoes, making it a good choice for an early spring or extended fall crop.

directions: A Siberian heirloom with soft, blue-green potato-leaf foliage that sets abundant clusters of translucent, pale-yellow, one-inch cherry tomatoes with a rich, sweet flavor. Bred for a short, cool growing season, Galina's sets fruit reliably in cooler spring and fall conditions that cause many other cherry tomatoes to drop blossoms, making it a strong choice for a Gulf South fall tomato planting timed to ripen as temperatures moderate. The prolific, early-bearing vines need only routine staking and produce continuously from first ripe fruit until frost.
sources: Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds Variety Catalog

common_name: Snow White Cherry Tomato (Pale Ivory Sweet Cherry)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6 weeks before the last frost; transplant after frost danger passes and stake or cage the vines, watering consistently once fruit sets to reduce cracking of the thin, pale skin.

directions: A pale ivory-yellow cherry tomato with such low acidity and high sugar that it is regularly ranked among the sweetest cherry tomatoes grown, with a near-translucent skin over blushing golden flesh. The heavy-yielding indeterminate vines set long clusters of one-inch round fruit continuously through the season and benefit from steady, even watering, since the thin skin cracks readily after a dry spell followed by heavy rain. Its mild, sugary flavor and pastel color make it a favorite for fresh eating and mixed cherry-tomato salads rather than cooking.
sources: Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds Variety Catalog
